name: Incus / LXD
author: Netlens
description: Shows an Incus (or LXD) server or cluster: the servers as hosts and every container and virtual machine as a guest, with state, MAC and IP addresses (when the instance sits on your LAN rather than behind NAT), image, CPU and memory limits, and autostart. Read-only: it only sends GET requests with a client certificate that you add to the trust store as restricted.

info.title: Make a client certificate (once)
info.text: Incus authenticates API clients with a certificate. Make one, give the server a listening address, trust the certificate (restricted: read-only is enough because Netlens only reads) and paste the two files below. LXD works the same with 'lxc'.
info.code:
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout netlens.key -out netlens.crt -days 3650 -subj "/CN=netlens"
incus config set core.https_address :8443
incus config trust add-certificate netlens.crt --name netlens --restricted

config.label: Incus servers
config.help: One line per server or cluster (one cluster member is enough, it lists the others).

columns.label: Client certificate (PEM)
columns.help: The whole text of netlens.crt, from -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- to -----END CERTIFICATE-----.

config.label: Verify the server's certificate
config.help: Incus makes its own self-signed server certificate; leave this off unless you installed a trusted one.
